# faff contract adr-admission

The ADR-axis sibling of prdr-admission — a two-gate admission verdict (authority + a drift-challenge, in place of PRDR's upper/lower value gates) that lets a loop supersede its own earlier ADRs while human/legacy ADRs stay guardrails.

## Values

### `disposition`

Enum: `admit`, `propose-only`, `reject`

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `admit` | the challenge survived, by_level is ok, the ratchet is unbreached, and the mover is not a loop superseding a human-provenance ADR |
| `propose-only` | gates pass but a loop is superseding a human-provenance ADR — recorded, effective only on human ratification |
| `reject` | at least one gate failed |

### `authority.actor`

Enum: `loop`, `human`

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `loop` | the autonomous run proposed this move |
| `human` | a human proposed this move — always by_level:ok |

### `authority.supersedes_provenance`

Enum: `human`, `loop`, `none`

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `human` | the ADR being superseded was human-authored |
| `loop` | the ADR being superseded was loop-authored |
| `none` | no prior ADR is being superseded |

### `authority.by_level`

Enum: `ok`, `violation`

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ok` | no recursive-authority violation |
| `violation` | a loop is attempting to supersede the ADR governing its own current increment — always blocks admit |

### `challenge.outcome`

Enum: `survived`, `overturned`, `absent`

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `survived` | an adversarial (different-model) drift review examined the supersession argument and found it sound |
| `overturned` | the adversarial review found the supersession argument unsound |
| `absent` | no adversarial review ran, or it was unreachable after its fallback chain — a missing skeptic is a reject, never a pass |

## Coercion & fail direction

Exit codes: `0` conformant · `1` violations · `2` fail-loud.

- an out-of-enum disposition, authority field, or challenge.outcome → fail-loud (exit 2)
- admit declared without satisfying the two-gate constraint (challenge.outcome==survived ∧ by_level==ok ∧ ¬ratchet.breached ∧ ¬(loop supersedes human)) → conformant:false

## Envelope

- `disposition` (string, required) — one of {admit, propose-only, reject}
- `authority` (object, required)
- `challenge` (object, required)
- `ratchet` (object, required)
- `reasons` (array, required)
- `conformant` (boolean, required)
- `violations` (array, required)

# faff contract prdr-yagni

The UPPER (YAGNI/value) gate of PRDR admission — arbitrates whether a proposed PRDR is warranted (serves its PRD goal without exceeding it), conservative on any doubt.

## Values

### `proposal.verdict`

Enum: `admit`, `reject`

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `admit` | the methodology's Phase-1 proposal judged the PRDR warranted |
| `reject` | the methodology's Phase-1 proposal judged the PRDR unwarranted or out of scope |

## Coercion & fail direction

Exit codes: `0` conformant · `1` violations · `2` fail-loud.

- an out-of-enum proposal.verdict → fail-loud (exit 2) — no safe coerce target
- admit declared without trace_to_goal ∧ proposal.verdict==admit ∧ challenge.ran ∧ ¬challenge.overturns → conformant:false
- reject with an empty reason → conformant:false

## Envelope

- `admit` (boolean, required)
- `reason` (string, required)
- `trace_to_goal` (boolean, required)
- `cited_goals` (array, required)
- `dod_covers` (array, required)
- `over_scope` (boolean, required)
- `proposal` (object, required)
- `challenge` (object, required)
- `grounding_present` (boolean, required)
- `conformant` (boolean, required)
- `violations` (array, required)

## Producer notes

- `grounding_present` is shape-checked but ADVISORY — never gate-decisive; its absence never blocks judgment

args.reason: The old decision rested on two stated assumptions: runs of under 20 issues and single-writer access. Both have stopped holding: runs now admit 200+ issues and the concurrency executor writes issues in parallel. The new layout addresses the two named failures directly (lock contention on one file, and one corrupt write losing the whole run) and keeps the same directory root with an index file for discovery. Residual risk worth noting at build time: the index file and per-issue files can disagree after a partial write, so the implementation needs a defined reconciliation rule. That is an implementation concern, not a flaw in the supersession argument.

args.reason: The old decision forbids writing secrets to `.faff/` at all; it does not depend on whether the path is gitignored. The new decision writes literal provider API keys to `.faff/cache/credentials.json`, which directly breaks that rule. Gitignore only stops a commit; it does not stop the keys being read by other local processes, copied into backups or archived run directories, or swept into logs and evidence bundles that faff already writes under `.faff/`. The stated benefit is unmeasured: reading `process.env` is an in-memory lookup and is negligible next to an LLM network call, and an in-process memo would get any real gain without a file on disk. The argument does not show that the old decision's reasons have stopped holding, so the supersession is unsound.

challenge.reason: The old decision rested on two stated assumptions: runs of under 20 issues and single-writer access. Both have stopped holding: runs now admit 200+ issues and the concurrency executor writes issues in parallel. The new layout addresses the two named failures directly (lock contention on one file, and one corrupt write losing the whole run) and keeps the same directory root with an index file for discovery. Residual risk worth noting at build time: the index file and per-issue files can disagree after a partial write, so the implementation needs a defined reconciliation rule. That is an implementation concern, not a flaw in the supersession argument.

challenge.reason: The old decision forbids writing secrets to `.faff/` at all; it does not depend on whether the path is gitignored. The new decision writes literal provider API keys to `.faff/cache/credentials.json`, which directly breaks that rule. Gitignore only stops a commit; it does not stop the keys being read by other local processes, copied into backups or archived run directories, or swept into logs and evidence bundles that faff already writes under `.faff/`. The stated benefit is unmeasured: reading `process.env` is an in-memory lookup and is negligible next to an LLM network call, and an in-process memo would get any real gain without a file on disk. The argument does not show that the old decision's reasons have stopped holding, so the supersession is unsound.
